Opted into the v8 sparse-transient-cap mode from the start; none of the three PRED_TP tracks ("Black Is the Color," "Anna May," "Learn About Love") needed more than a fraction of a dB of recovery, under the threshold where capping is worth attempting, so all three land at their honest linear-reduced targets instead. Three titles restored to the archive's established spelling after the fresh export drifted: "I Need a Lover" to "Hear Me," "I Want to Lean About Love" to "Learn About Love," and the recurring slash/hyphen filename convention on "The Kiss / Da Da Da (Slave to an Angel)." A typo in track 27's filename ("Barney" for "Blarney") was also corrected.

item.title: Reprocessed 12 of the 29 tracks on Jerry Hannan's solo show at 19 Broadway from June 7, 1…
item.description: Reprocessed 12 of the 29 tracks on Jerry Hannan's solo show at 19 Broadway from June 7, 1999 to the sparse-transient-cap mode (v5→v8) — the archive's first scoped reprocess, touching only the tracks that actually needed it rather than the whole show. The other 17 tracks were already at their loudness target under the older workflow and gained nothing from a fresh render, so they were left untouched. Five capped tracks needed a listen before shipping and all checked out as legitimate music, not defects: “Kilkelly Ireland” (0:20.45), “Butter” (0:39.45), “Everything Reminds Me of You” (3:53.90 and 4:34.50), “Happy Birthday Marco” (0:38.05, overlapping a suspected click already confirmed as music), and “Ted Kennedy Song” (0:02.20). Two more — “Hello in There” and “Hollywood (alt verse)” — initially declined the cap automatically for exceeding the calibrated review band (longer or denser engagement than the original listening evidence covered); after listening, both were given an explicit per-track override (“Hello in There” now reaches the full −20 target instead of −23.7; “Hollywood” recovers to −20.3, just short of full target since it hit the 6 dB attenuation ceiling). One title was corrected: the fresh export's filename read “Come On All You Young Maidens” for track 27, a completely different phrase from the archive's established title “A Bunch of Thyme” (also used on another show, and already named in this show's own description) — kept the established spelling. That track's audio was already at its target from the original v5 pass, so only the local filename needed correcting, not a reprocess.

item.title: Reprocessed Jerry Hannan's solo show at 19 Broadway from February 1, 1999 under the new w…
item.description: Reprocessed Jerry Hannan's solo show at 19 Broadway from February 1, 1999 under the new workflow (v8), replacing the show's v5 pass — the whole-show noise reduction from that earlier pass (6dB, sensitivity 5) carries over unchanged. Five of the twenty-one tracks qualify for the sparse-transient-cap mode, reaching the full −20 LUFS target instead of landing quieter; a sixth, “The Grey Funnel Line,” stays on the existing applause-only limiter. “Perfect Autumn Day” needed a listen before shipping and checked out as legitimate music. “Hello in There” needed 6.2 dB of recovery, just over the archive's standard 6 dB ceiling; a loudness-matched review of the gap found no meaningful risk at that size, so it was given an explicit one-track exception and now reaches −20.9 instead of the −26.2 it would have landed at otherwise. Two other flagged moments were checked and aren't defects: “Daddy”'s mid-song high-crest window at 1:15 is mic handling noise, not applause or clipping, and is capped along with the rest of the track's transients; “Everything Reminds Me of You”'s suspected click at 2:50.6 is an audience clap, not a digital defect. “Blind Man” has a real gap in the tape around 3:10 that noise reduction and splitting can't repair — flagged on the show page and left for a future Audacity pass rather than papered over. Three track titles carry a guest performer's name in their filename only, matching the archive's existing convention for this show (title stays clean, credit goes in the artist field): “Long Black Veil,” “The Grey Funnel Line” (both with Sean Hannan), and “Drift Away” (with Demir). One title was corrected — the fresh export's filename read “Angel of Montgomery,” the same mechanical typo already caught on another show; kept the established spelling “Angel from Montgomery.”

item.title: Gave “The Wind” an explicit, one-off exception to the archive's standard 6 dB transient-c…
item.description: Gave “The Wind” an explicit, one-off exception to the archive's standard 6 dB transient-cap ceiling, reaching the full −20 LUFS target instead of the −22.65 it landed at yesterday. The track's loudest moment (1:37.50, a vocal peak) needs 8.65 dB of recovery — over the usual limit — but a loudness-matched listening test at 6/8/10 dB of cut depth on that exact moment, plus the real full-target render, found no audible difference from the standard treatment. This is a per-track decision, not a policy change: the engine now records the exact ceiling used for every capped track (`policy_max_gr_db`) and flags any track exceeding the standard 6 dB as an explicit `override`, so this exception — and any future one — stays auditable without relying on memory or free-text notes. No other track in the archive is affected; the archive-wide ceiling remains 6 dB.

item.title: Reprocessed Jerry Hannan's solo show at 19 Broadway from March 29, 1999 under the new wor…
item.description: Reprocessed Jerry Hannan's solo show at 19 Broadway from March 29, 1999 under the new workflow (v8), replacing the show's v2 pass — the last remaining show in the archive on the original engine. This was also the show whose Drive noise-reduction export had gone through two separate upload passes months apart, leaving 34 stale duplicate files from the first pass sitting alongside the final corrected export; those were identified by timestamp and cleared before this run. Twenty-nine of the thirty-four tracks needed help beyond plain linear gain: five are handled by the applause-only limiter and sixteen qualify for the sparse-transient-cap mode, reaching the full −20 LUFS target instead of landing quieter. Three tracks' capped moments were confirmed by ear before shipping: “The Wind” (~1% of the track across several short events, e.g. 0:22.95 and 0:39.75), “The Bold Fenian Men” at 1:22.35, and “Hello in There” at 2:31.30 — all legitimate music, not defects. Two suspected digital defects were also checked by ear and confirmed as music, not clicks: “Blind Man” at 3:07.702 and “The Parting Glass” at 2:52.138. One title was restored to the archive's established spelling — “I Need a Lover” to “Hear Me” — and track 30, freshly retitled “Limerick Medley” from the prior catalog's “Some Get Married for Love,” was confirmed correct by ear rather than by cross-reference, since neither title matched anything else in the archive.

item.description: Reprocessed Jerry Hannan's solo show at 19 Broadway from January 15, 2001 under the new workflow (v8), replacing the show's v7 pass. Twenty-one of the set's thirty-one songs qualified for the sparse-transient-cap mode shipped last night — reaching the archive's full −20 LUFS target instead of landing several dB quieter — while “Woman” stayed on the existing applause-only limiter, where a burst of clapping rather than the music sets the ceiling. The fresh hand-edit export used different track names than the archive's established titles for four songs — “State Trooper,” “Everything,” “Four Leaf Clover Inn,” and “Never Knew a Woman” — restored to “Highway Patrolman,” “Everything Reminds Me of You,” “The Barney Stone Blues,” and “Woman” rather than overwritten.

item.title: Reprocessed this Mad Hannans set at Cafe Java again, this time under a new workflow (v8) …
item.description: Reprocessed this Mad Hannans set at Cafe Java again, this time under a new workflow (v8) built for tapes where the mic sat close to the drums: a millisecond-scale true-peak limiter now catches only the sharpest instant of an isolated musical transient — a snare hit, a strum — while the surrounding performance keeps its full, untouched gain, letting more tracks reach the archive's −20 LUFS standard instead of landing several dB quieter. Fifteen of the twenty-two tracks qualified and are now capped this way; “Rocky Road to Dublin / Star of County Down” needed more recovery than the policy's 6 dB ceiling allows, so it lands at −21.6 LUFS instead of −20 — inaudibly quieter, never over-shaved. “Truck” and “Anna May” are untouched by this change: both were already correctly handled by an earlier, unrelated fix that limits only audience applause at a track's edges, not the music. Two titles also picked up small spelling corrections back to the archive's established convention: “ABC (alt version)” and “The Kiss / Da Da Da (Slave to an Angel).”

item.title: Re-normalized this Mad Hannans set at Cafe Java to −20 LUFS on the current audio engineer…
item.description: Re-normalized this Mad Hannans set at Cafe Java to −20 LUFS on the current audio engineering workflow (v7), replacing the show's original v1 pass — the last v1 show in the archive. The fresh hand-edit pass applied noise reduction across the show and corrected the song list: what was catalogued as a single 5:39 track, “Everything Reminds Me of You,” is in fact two songs, now split into separate tracks with the second restored as “Hear Me” — so the show runs 22 tracks rather than 21. “My Dear” has been identified as the song the archive lists elsewhere as “Ride On” and retitled to match, and “Plastic Melons” corrected to “Plastic Lemons.” Elsewhere in the archive, two tracks catalogued as “I Need a Lover” have been corrected to “Hear Me,” the song's real title.

item.description: Re-normalized all 21 tracks of this Mad Hannans set at the Sweetwater to −20 LUFS on the current audio engineering workflow (v7), replacing the show's original v2 pass; re-exported track 14 ("Butter") to restore the song's opening chords, missing from an earlier transfer; also corrected drifted titles "Hard Drinking," "I Need a Lover," and "The Kiss / Da Da Da (Slave to an Angel)" back to the archive's established convention, using the automated audio engineering workflow with ffmpeg.

item.title: Brought four more pre-v4 shows up to the current processing engine (v7) — Jerry Hannan at…
item.description: Brought four more pre-v4 shows up to the current processing engine (v7) — Jerry Hannan at 19 Broadway on 1999-05-10, 1999-06-21, 1999-07-19, and 2001-01-15 — replacing early loudnorm-based passes that had occasionally fallen back to dynamic-mode compression instead of true linear gain. All four re-split from fresh hand-edit exports and re-verified against R2.
